source.citation: Lutz, M. P., Zimmerman, R. W. (2005). Effect of an inhomogeneous interphase zone on the bulk modulus and conductivity of a particulate composite. International Journal of Solids and Structures 42(2), 429-437.
source.location: Eq. (5), p. 431; Section 3 and Fig. 2, p. 433; Section 4 and Fig. 3, p. 436

transcription.from: the published article (PDF): Eq. (5) and the text that describes Figs. 2 and 3, read on the page text
transcription.note: Only the parameters of the two examples are transcribed; no value is read on the curves of the figures.

profile_exponent.description: Integer exponent b of the profile of Eq. (5), K(r) = K_m + (K_if - K_m) (r/a)^(-b) and the same for the shear modulus, a being the radius of the inclusion; b = 10 is an interphase whose thickness is about one eighth of the diameter of the inclusion.

stiffness_contrast.location: Section 3 and caption of Fig. 2, p. 433
stiffness_contrast.description: Ratio of the moduli of the inclusion to those of the pure matrix, K_i / K_m.

poisson_ratio.location: Section 3 and caption of Fig. 2, p. 433
poisson_ratio.description: Poisson ratio, the same in the matrix, in the interphase and in the inclusion.

conductivity_contrast.description: Ratio of the conductivity of the inclusion to that of the pure matrix, in the example of Fig. 3.

notes: Table interphase_contrasts: the values of D = (K_m - K_if) / K_m that label the curves of Fig. 2, p. 433 (the same parameter is defined on the conductivities in Fig. 3).
The profile reaches the moduli of the pure matrix at infinity only; the article solves the hydrostatic and the conduction problems for it in series.
